title: Combining Functions with Built-In Modules knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which mental model best explains “Combining Functions with Built-In Modules” in Dart Sass?
options: The best solution is always to replace native CSS behavior with a new Sass abstraction.

Dart Sass groups built-ins into namespaced modules such as `sass:math`, `sass:color`, `sass:list`, `sass:map`, `sass:string`, `sass:meta`, and `sass:selector`. Load the module you need and read its argument and return-value contract.
The browser executes Sass source directly, so a compilation step is unnecessary.
Readable SCSS guarantees correct browser rendering, accessibility, and performance without output review.
questions.answer_key: Dart Sass groups built-ins into namespaced modules such as `sass:math`, `sass:color`, `sass:list`, `sass:map`, `sass:string`, `sass:meta`, and `sass:selector`. Load the module you need and read its argument and return-value contract.
questions.explanation: Dart Sass groups built-ins into namespaced modules such as `sass:math`, `sass:color`, `sass:list`, `sass:map`, `sass:string`, `sass:meta`, and `sass:selector`. Load the module you need and read its argument and return-value contract. The alternative choices confuse Sass compilation with browser execution or claim guarantees that require independent tests.

questions.prompt: When applying “Math functions”, which approach is the most reliable?
options: A Sass function should return a value that can be used in an expression. Keep side effects out of its purpose and report missing or invalid input clearly.
Skip compilation and infer the final selector list and property values from the source file alone.
Prefer deeply nested selectors because fewer source lines always mean simpler and safer CSS.
Silence every warning before determining whether it identifies a deprecated or incorrect construct.
questions.answer_key: A Sass function should return a value that can be used in an expression. Keep side effects out of its purpose and report missing or invalid input clearly.
questions.explanation: A Sass function should return a value that can be used in an expression. Keep side effects out of its purpose and report missing or invalid input clearly. Compare the compiled output with the stated intent and preserve browser-native behavior where it is required.

questions.prompt: Which review decision most directly supports maintainability for “Combining Functions with Built-In Modules”?
options: Generate every possible selector or theme combination, even when most variants are never used.
Treat successful compilation as proof that the interface is accessible and behaves correctly in every browser.
Expose internal implementation details as public API and postpone documentation until after release.

Keep compiler-time calculations separate from CSS functions that should run in the browser. Test missing keys, invalid indices, unit compatibility, and color-space assumptions instead of hiding errors behind a fallback.

Test missing keys, invalid indices, unit compatibility, and color-space assumptions instead of hiding errors behind a fallback. The other choices increase output, assume unverified behavior, or make the public interface harder to maintain.
